title: The Thorn of Caerlum
premise: Marguerite Hartwell's gift for hearing the dead through the bones he carves has kept him alive and invisible in the smuggler's warrens of Thornfell—until the crown's witch-hunters arrive with a relic that can detect the gifted. Forced to guide a doomed royal expedition to the last dragon-fire beneath Caerlum, Marguerite discovers the dead are whispering a single warning: the fire is not dying, it is being caged, and the cage was built by his own ancestors. Torn between loyalty to the smuggler family that raised him and the truth the dead demand he speak, Marguerite must choose whether to shatter the cage and reignite the ancient dragon war—or let the last flame gutter out and take every bone-hearer with it.
about_author: Noor Delacroix is the pen name of a former stonemason who spent a decade restoring cathedral gargoyles before turning to fiction. They live in a converted signal tower on the coast, where they claim the wind still carries voices worth writing down.

chapters.title: The Bone-Carver's Quiet
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the mountain town of Hollowmere, Marguerite carves a dead woman's femur into a keepsake and hears her final secret—a hidden cache of smuggled salt. The beat establishes his double life: beloved craftsman by day, keeper of the dead's confidences by night, and utterly alone in knowing what he knows.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Crossroads
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Crown riders nail up a decree: all bone-hearers must surrender for 'sanctification.' A neighbor Marguerite quietly warned is taken anyway, screaming his name as they drag her off. Emotional beat: guilt—the first crack in his belief that silence and small kindnesses can keep everyone safe.

chapters.title: The Relic That Listens Back
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Seraphine Voss's POV. Voss demonstrates the Chirurgeon's Bell, a relic that rings when the gifted are near, to her reluctant escort of soldiers. She executes a suspected hearer to prove the bell works. Beat: cold conviction masking doubt—Voss heard something in the bell's tone she cannot explain.

chapters.title: Salt Roads and Old Debts
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The smuggler clan that raised him, led by his foster-mother Brannoc, orders him to guide a mysterious paying expedition over the Thornfell passes before winter seals them. He recognizes one client's crest: the crown. Beat: trapped between refusing and betraying the only family he has.

chapters.title: The Expedition Assembles
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge at the pass gate: Voss with her bell, a disgraced royal cartographer named Ellery Finch, and soldiers who fear the mountains more than witches. Marguerite signs on under a false name. Beat: dread sharpened by curiosity—he can hear the dead murmuring about Caerlum, and they sound afraid.

chapters.title: What the Pass Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Leading the column through a defile littered with ancient battle-bones, Marguerite hears a chorus of the war-dead describing dragons fighting beside humans—not against them. He nearly drops his pack when the Chirurgeon's Bell hums. Beat: wonder curdling into terror as history contradicts everything he was taught.

chapters.title: The Bell Rings True
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The bell tolls; Voss narrows suspects to the quiet carver traveling under a false name. Instead of arresting him, she tests him privately—and he lies so smoothly she almost believes him. Beat: a duel of masks; Voss begins to suspect the bell detects not the gift but something older beneath it.

chapters.title: Finch's Map Has Two Layers
chapters.summary: Ellery Finch's POV. The cartographer reveals to Marguerite that the royal route ends at Caerlum's sealed vault, and that his map shows a second, older route drawn in a hand identical to Marguerite's own carving style. Beat: vertigo of inheritance—the ancestors whose bones he handles built the cage around the dragon-fire.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Price
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Brannoc intercepts the column with smugglers disguised as bandits, offering Marguerite escape—if he abandons the clients and lets the expedition die in the snow. He refuses; she disowns him on the mountainside. Beat: the cost of choosing truth over belonging, paid in full and publicly.

chapters.title: Avalanche of Voices
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. An avalanche buries part of the column; digging survivors out, Marguerite uses his gift openly to find heartbeats through the bones of the dead beneath him. Soldiers see. Beat: exposure—but also the first moment of respect, as the men he saved look at him differently than the law says they should.

chapters.title: Sanctification
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Protocol demands arrest; instead Voss interrogates Marguerite through the night and hears the war-dead's testimony secondhand. Her faith wobbles against evidence. She chains him anyway, because the alternative is her own execution. Beat: duty as a prison both of them now share.

chapters.title: The Guttering Light
chapters.summary: Ellery Finch's POV. Nearing Caerlum, the party sees the northern sky dimming—the last dragon-fire is visibly failing, and frost creeps unnaturally down from the peaks. Villages along the way are emptying. Beat: stakes made planetary; this is no longer a hunt but a countdown.

chapters.title: Caerlum's Gate
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The vault door answers only to bone-hearers; Marguerite opens it under guard, hearing his ancestors' voices layered in the stone like sediment. Inside: a vast forge-cage around a coiled, sleeping ember-dragon no bigger than a horse. Beat: awe and horror—the 'ancient enemy' is a prisoner, not a threat.

chapters.title: The Cage-Makers' Confession
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, deep-echo chapter. Touching the cage-bones, Marguerite receives the full ancestral memory: his forebears caged the dragon-fire to hoard its power, birthing the witch-hunts to eliminate anyone who might free it. Beat: shame transmuted into resolve—the secret could reignite war only if kept.

chapters.title: Orders from the Throne
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. A royal dispatch arrives: drain the fire into a portable reliquary and kill the dragon. Voss realizes the crown manufactured the entire crisis. Beat: her crisis of loyalty—obey and become the corruption she hunted, or defy and die a traitor.

chapters.title: Mutiny at the Forge
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The soldiers split; some follow the reliquary order, others side with Marguerite after Finch publishes the ancestral confession via his maps. Fighting breaks out inside the vault as the fire gutters faster. Beat: chaos as every faction's mask burns away; Finch dies holding the doorway open.

chapters.title: The Choice of Bones
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. To free the dragon, someone must join their voice to the cage-bones permanently—the dead have been asking all along, and Marguerite finally understands why his gift exists. He begins the carving of his own life into the lock. Beat: sacrifice embraced without melodrama; grief and certainty braided together.

chapters.title: Voss's Verdict
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss arrives at the lock intending to stop him, bell raised—and instead rings it herself, shattering it, using the relic's stored resonance to complete what Marguerite started. Beat: redemption through betrayal of her masters; the hunter becomes the key.

chapters.title: Dragonfire Rekindled
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, half-translucent. The cage breaks; the ember-dragon blazes to full size, and the dead of ten thousand years sing through Marguerite as he becomes the bridge between species. Beat: climax—war does not reignite; the lie that demanded it burns away instead.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Ash and Snow
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The surviving column descends to find spring thawing early; the crown's hunters are recalled in disgrace. Voss surrenders herself to testify, expecting the scaffold, and finds the soldiers who saw the dragon will stand witness. Beat: exhausted hope; accountability beginning.

chapters.title: The Carver Who Became a Door
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Brannoc climbs to Caerlum seeking her lost son and finds him changed—alive but threaded with the dead's chorus, no longer wholly hers nor wholly himself. Their reconciliation is imperfect and real. Beat: belonging redefined rather than restored; family as choice renewed.

chapters.title: First Fire, Last Chapter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Months later, Marguerite teaches other hearers openly in rebuilt Hollowmere, carving bones that carry comfort instead of secrets, while the dragon circles the peaks like a promise. Final line lands on the theme: power shared corrupts nothing; power hoarded never survives the winter. Beat: quiet, earned resolution.
